note: Rewritten from the original description by Snyder (1929); the original is in English. The deutated adult is the holotype; the soldier was described from 2 specimens taken in the same series as the holotype. The original records that this genus had not previously been recorded from the Antilles, this species being the first record.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A medium-sized tree termite. Soldier body length 5.5—6.5 mm, head length including mandibles 2.4—2.5 mm, head length excluding mandibles 1.8—1.9 mm, head width 1.2—1.4 mm, pronotum width 1.1—1.4 mm; antennae 10 or 11 segments, slightly longer than the mandibles. Alate body length without wings 4.75—5.75 mm, head width (including eyes) 1.1—1.2 mm, eye diameter 0.302 mm, ocelli large and round, closely adjacent to the compound eyes. The original notes that its boring galleries resemble those of Cryptotermes; the faecal pellets are small, rather slender, irregularly shaped and pointed at the ends, like apple seeds.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head deep chestnut-brown to pitch-black, smooth and shining, arched, nearly as wide as long, highest in the middle, posterior margin rounded, sparsely clothed with long pale-yellow hairs. Antennae pale chestnut-brown (broken in the specimen), each segment widening towards the apex, clothed with long hairs; segment 1 long cylindrical; segment 2 shorter than 1 but longer than 3, subclavate; segment 3 more wedge-shaped; segments after the fifth lengthening. Apical segment of maxillary palp long cylindrical, pointed at the tip. Compound eyes black, slightly protruding, not circular, the distance to the lateral margin of the head less than their diameter. Ocelli large, round, closely adjoining the compound eyes. Labrum yellowish brown, wider than long, broadly rounded at the apex, widest in the middle, clothed with long hairs. Pronotum concolorous with the head, more than twice as wide as long, anterior margin concave, posterior margin convex, sides rounded, sloping gradually to the posterior margin, margins with long hairs. Posterior margins of meso- and metanotum concave. Wing scales longer than the pronotum, clothed with long hairs. Legs pale yellowish brown, tibiae darker, rather slender, hairy; apex of tibia with 3 spines. Abdomen paler than the pronotum, still paler ventrally, margins with long, dense pale-yellow hairs and short hairs; styli present. Measurements: total length of the alate without wings 4.75—5.75 mm (the smaller being dried specimens); head length 1.3—1.4 mm; pronotum length 0.6—0.7 mm; hind tibia length 1—1.005+ mm; head width (including eyes) 1.1—1.2 mm; eye diameter 0.302 mm; pronotum width 1.1—1.4 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellowish brown, darker and deeply cleft anteriorly, longer than wide but relatively short, subcylindrical, slightly narrowed anteriorly, highest in the middle; frontal face edged with black, nearly vertical, scattered with long pale-yellow hairs, with a row of 4 long hairs in the middle of the dorsum, the inner 2 slightly shorter than the outer 2, and another row of hairs on the anterior part of the head. Antennae pale yellowish brown, 10 or 11 segments, slightly longer than the mandibles, clothed with long hairs, each segment widening towards the apex; segment 1 long cylindrical; segment 2 shorter than 1, not clavate; segment 3 longer than 2, clavate, appearing subdivided near the base; segment 4 wider, shorter than 3; apical segment slender, subelliptical. Compound eyes pale, large, slender, subelliptical, situated near the antennal sockets. Labrum yellowish brown, longer than wide, somewhat ligulate, rounded at the apex, with 2 long hairs at the middle of the apex that are longer than the labrum, and with short hairs. Mandibles black, short, shorter than the head width, broad at the base, pointed and incurved at the apex; left mandible with 2 small sharp marginal teeth near the apex and 1 broader tooth near the base; right mandible with 2 broader marginal teeth near the base. Postmentum slender, narrowed in the middle, the anterior width less than twice the middle width. Pronotum paler than the head, twice as wide as long, anterior and posterior margins nearly parallel, anterior angles high, sides rounded, sloping gradually posteriorly, margins with long pale-yellow hairs. Tibiae and tarsi pale yellow, rather slender, femora thickened. Abdomen greyish white, clothed with long, dense pale-yellow hairs. Measurements: soldier body length 5.5—6.5 mm; head length including mandibles 2.4—2.5 mm; head length excluding mandibles 1.8—1.9 mm; left mandible length 0.85 mm; pronotum length (to the angles) 0.65—0.80 mm; hind tibia length 0.57—0.705 mm; head width 1.2—1.4 mm; pronotum width 1.1—1.4 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality Aibonito, Puerto Rico. On 2 December 1921 (month 12), F. Sein and George N. Wolcott collected several deutated adults from a half-dead coffee tree (collection number 488-'21), together with 2 soldiers and several nymphs; the holotype (a deutated adult) is in the United States National Museum, Cat. No. 25415, U.S.N.M. Its galleries in the dry, hard, sound wood of the half-dead coffee trunk resemble those of Cryptotermes; the faecal pellets are small, rather slender, irregularly shaped and pointed at the ends like apple seeds.
